public_rationale: The evidence supports recurring model maintenance and substantial growth in broader compute spending. It does not cleanly measure the claimed training-cost increase or establish that the full expense is unavoidable. Experimental R&D, final training, and maintenance are different categories. The complete proposition remains unsettled; this is not a finding that training is a one-time expense.
limitations: The strongest spending series measures broader categories than the claim.
The maintenance example establishes a practice, not its financial scale.
Commercial necessity is harder to establish than recurring expenditure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM training costs are increasing dramatically and are an ongoing, unavoidable cost of doing business, not one-off R&D.

statement.excerpt: To be clear, all of this is well-known and documented, but the nomenclature of “training” suggests that it might stop one day, versus the truth: training costs are increasing dramatically, and “training” covers anything from training new models to bug fixes on existing ones. And, more fundamentally, it’s an ongoing cost — something that’s an essential and unavoidable cost of doing business.

from_speaker: training new models to bug fixes on existing ones
an essential and unavoidable cost of doing business
our_interpretation: Read this as a claim about frontier LLM developers continuing to develop and maintain competitive products, particularly OpenAI and Anthropic in the surrounding passage.
Use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual spending period before the post, with 2024 as the comparison baseline.
Read 'dramatically' as a large increase on a comparable basis; do not invent a precise percentage threshold.
Recurring expenditure can still be research and development. The quoted claim does not itself establish a GAAP cost-of-goods-sold classification.
Separate training and post-training from inference, total compute, and broader experimental R&D.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable expenditure histories show a large increase in training costs, and operational evidence establishes repeated training for new models and maintenance as a continuing requirement of these developers' businesses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable histories show training expenditure was stable or falling, or operational evidence establishes that the alleged continuing training requirement is materially absent.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI documents a behavioral problem in an update to an existing model and lists changes to training techniques among its remedies. This supports the maintenance component, but supplies no expenditure series or proof that all training expenditure is unavoidable.

evidence.explanation: Epoch distinguishes final training runs from the larger experimental research budget. The earlier-period analysis limits any inference that rising R&D compute is entirely recurring model maintenance.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable training and post-training expenditure histories, with maintenance separated from experimental research, and evidence explaining which recurring activities are necessary to sustain the businesses.
